title: Hang Seng Tech Index Sinks 40% From Peak in Worst Day Since April 2025

tickers.name: Alibaba Group Holding Limited American Depositary Shares, each represents eight Ordinary Shares

summary:
Chinese technology shares in Hong Kong experienced a dislocation on Oct. 22 that erased nearly all gains achieved following the September 24 economic stimulus event. The Hang Seng Tech Index fell 4.38% to approximately 3,834, recording its worst single-day performance since Trump's "Liberation Day" in April 2025. This rout has pushed the tech index more than 40% below its peak and lowered the group's forward P/E ratio to 13x, while the broader Hang Seng Index dropped 2.7% to fall below the 23,000 level.

The selloff concentrated in artificial intelligence stocks, with Tianshu Zhixin and Zhipu both dropping more than 9%, Iluvatar CoreX falling 6%, and SMIC declining more than 3%. Tencent traded below HK$400, with Alibaba and Lenovo also posting losses. Investors are pricing in margin pressures from a price war among Chinese AI labs, where models such as DeepSeek V4.1 Flash cost $0.15 per million input tokens, alongside AI spending concerns in Japan and Korea. Concurrently, a new government draft proposes export licenses for frontier AI models with over 2 trillion parameters or those trained with more than 10^26 FLOPs.

selectedTweets.text:
China's AI stocks are getting HIT in Hong Kong today.

The Hang Seng Tech Index fell about 4% to around 3,834, while the Hang Seng Index dropped almost 3%.

According to Chinese media, AI model makers MiniMax and Zhipu fell more than 4%, along with $BABA and Lenovo, while AI chip designer Iluvatar CoreX dropped 6% and SMIC fell more than 3%.

Tencent is now trading below HK$400.

Part of it is the same worry about AI spending that is weighing on Korea and Japan today.

But China also has its own problem because its AI labs are in a brutal price war, with models like DeepSeek V4.1 Flash now priced at about $0.15 per million input tokens.

That is great for usage, because cheaper AI means more of it but not so great for the margins of the companies selling the models, and the market is starting to price that in.
selectedTweets.quotedTweetText:
China wants to control exports of its most powerful AI models.

A new draft adds 23 AI technologies to its export control list, including large models, AI agents and computing clusters.

Frontier models above 2 trillion parameters, or trained with more than 10^26 FLOPs, would need a license before their weights or source code leave the country.

Open source models that are already public are exempt.
